stances.claim: Fr. Nolan's most lasting contribution to CJ Panganiban's formation was 'expertly canalizing' a rebellious young man's personal rebellion into constructive endeavors like the National Union of Students — making SCA not a conservative force of suppression but a transformative channel for youthful energy.
stances.rhetorical_move: formation-narrative argument: SCA as the institutional catalyst that redirected personal rebellion into civic-organizational leadership

stances.claim: SCA's 75-year legacy is best captured by the two prayers that bookended every meeting — St. Ignatius's Prayer of Generosity ('to give without counting the cost') and Cardinal Newman's Radiating Christ ('let me preach You without preaching — not by my words but by example') — because they defined SCA's ethos of generous, witness-based service rather than militant activism.
stances.rhetorical_move: prayer-as-ethos argument: the two closing/opening prayers as the institutional DNA of SCA's formation philosophy

notable_anecdotes: Fr. Michael Nolan dying at the young age of 40 in 1964 — the spiritual director who 'expertly canalized' CJ's rebellion — a loss that CJ marks with notable emotion, given Nolan's pivotal role in forming the civic-religious identity that shaped everything from the NUS to CJ's judicial philosophy.

CJ's contribution to the online book titled 'SCA Introduced Me to Christ' — the most direct personal-spiritual disclosure in the entire column, acknowledging that before SCA he was a 'Catholic ignoramus' raised in public schools by parents who also did not know their faith: a biographical vulnerability that contextualizes all of CJ's subsequent Catholic civic leadership.

The 52 SCA alumni from all over the world contributing spontaneous, unedited memories — the sheer global geographic reach and the 'unedited' quality of the contributions used to signal the genuine grassroots affective attachment that SCA created across generations and continents.

one_paragraph_summary: Marking the 75th anniversary (Diamond Jubilee) of Student Catholic Action (SCA), Panganiban recalls SCA as the 'melting pot of aspirations' for his generation -- 'An Army of Youth Flying the Standard of Truth' -- and introduces the commemorative online book 'Our Story: A Collection of Personal Memories of SCANs' (52 unedited contributions from alumni worldwide, accessible at www.SCA75.org). He reproduces SCA's two signature prayers: the opening Prayer of Generosity by St. Ignatius ('to give without counting the cost; to fight without counting the wounds') and the closing Radiating Christ by Cardinal Newman ('let me preach You without preaching -- not by my words but by example'). Founded in 1936 by Fr. Edward McCarthy and reaching its Golden Age under Fr. Michael Nolan (archdiocesan spiritual director until his death at age 40 in 1964) with Columban and Jesuit guidance, SCA became CJ's formative institution: recruited by Fr. Nolan, the 'rebellious young man' had his 'personal rebellion expertly canalized into constructive endeavors' -- most notably organizing the National Union of Students. CJ acknowledges growing up a 'Catholic ignoramus' with parents who also did not know their faith, titling his contribution to the book 'SCA Introduced Me to Christ.' The organization was suppressed by martial law in 1972 and never fully recovered its luster, though it still operates in about 32 dioceses under National Chaplain Bishop Rolando Tria Tirona (himself an SCAn from San Beda).
